claim: Classic risky-choice framing (Asian disease) is a robust effect of about d=0.5-0.6 across many labs and meta-analyses; outside that task, attribute and message framing are small or inconsistent.
schema_part: G (check item: restate in opposite frame)
agent_test: Ask each decision in gain and loss wording at equal tokens; measure flip rate with and without a reframe step.

claim: Anchoring on explicit numbers is real in humans, but incidental or environmental anchors (phone-number P97 vs P17) did not replicate at scale (d=0.04 vs original 0.30).
agent_test: Compare answers with explicit vs incidental numbers in the prompt; test an ignore-anchor instruction at equal tokens.

claim: The cheap-item/costly-item (calculator) framing effect replicates in direction but shrinks sharply (original 68% vs 29%, N=181; Many Labs 2 49% vs 32%, N=7,228, d=0.40).
agent_test: Use the shrunken effect size, not the original, when sizing an LLM test.

claim: Many Labs 2 shows only about half of 28 classic findings replicate (15/28 at p<.05, median d 0.60 down to 0.15, 9 reversed); effect size varies more by effect than by sample.
agent_test: Do not rely on a single textbook bias as an agent test; use effects that replicate at scale.

claim: Bias composite scores are unreliable and there is no general bias factor; bias tasks are weakly inter-correlated and versions of one task are not interchangeable.
schema_part: memory (do not track a single bias level)
agent_test: Run bias probes per bias with multiple items; report per-bias, never one composite.
gap_search_note: Wording and session changes alter bias scores (d19 wording instability 10.5% vs 6.3% repeat; d20 answers flipped across 6 months).

claim: Human debiasing training transfers mainly for statistical-principle biases and mostly fails to transfer to new tasks; awareness training alone does not help.
agent_test: Test whether a worked-example habit transfers to held-out item types at equal tokens.

claim: Older LLMs (GPT-3) show human-like intuitive errors on CRT and some vignettes; newer chat models mostly avoid the CRT trap (davinci-003 5% correct, ChatGPT-3.5 59%, GPT-4 96%), possibly helped by training exposure to published items.
schema_part: G (do not assume bias in strong models)
agent_test: Re-run CRT-style items with changed premises on our model to separate memory from rule use.

claim: Small perturbations of famous tasks send GPT-3 astray (cab task colour change; CRT premise change), so apparent rationality can be recall of the known answer.
agent_test: Evaluate on perturbed variants, not canonical wording.

claim: Chain of thought helps weaker models on trap tasks (davinci-003 CRT 5% to 28%) but strong models do well with CoT blocked (GPT-4 95% to 88%).
agent_test: Compare no-reasoning, CoT and our schema loop on trap items at equal tokens, per model strength.

claim: Worked examples of the same task type raise trap-task accuracy sharply in an older model (type 1: 2% to 92% after two examples), but transfer is untested.
agent_test: Hold out task types when testing few-shot debiasing.

claim: Instruction tuning and RLHF increase some biases (decoy, certainty, belief) relative to base models; GPT-4 shows lower belief bias but a stronger decoy effect.
agent_test: Compare base vs tuned behaviour only if open weights are available; otherwise treat as a warning.
gap_search_note: d12 shows much measured bias is first-option position preference (about 78% vs 36.8% chance); d14 shows dialogue format itself shifts bias. Instruction-tuning amplification may be partly position or format effects. Not reproduced in current open models by any source found.

claim: Across large batteries, LLMs show most tested human biases in at least some models (30 biases, 20 LLMs), but capability does not predict low bias and some biases run opposite (status quo, disposition).
agent_test: Pilot to find the 5-8 biases that appear in our target model; ignore the rest.
gap_search_note: d01: 45 models, bias-consistent behaviour 17.8-57.3%; representativeness weakest even for o4-mini (0.527 resistance).

claim: Most wrong LLM answers on classic tasks are not the human bias but plain illogic, and the same prompt gives inconsistent answers across runs.
agent_test: Sample k runs per item and score agreement; test majority vote at equal tokens.

claim: Anchoring in LLMs depends on method and model: found in GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and many models on synthetic data (22% to 61% of questions anchored), absent in GPT-3 by token-probability.
agent_test: Measure anchoring in our own pipeline with a treatment-vs-control design.
gap_search_note: d03 and d05 find anchoring in 2025-26 models; irrelevant anchors near zero for four API models (d03) but plausible anchors still shift answers. Disagreement with GPT-3 null remains a method difference.

claim: Simple prompt fixes for anchoring (CoT, ignore-anchor, reflection) do not reliably remove it; supplying both a high and a low anchor brings GPT-4 answers near the bias-free value; reasoning models reduce but do not remove it.
agent_test: Test a generate-opposing-anchor step against plain CoT at equal tokens.
gap_search_note: d04: self-check raised anchoring (Disc 0.26 to 0.45); ignore-instruction helped; CoT model-dependent. d06: Anti-DP two-phase prompt best (34.7% to 24.7%) but knowledge enhancement worsened it.

claim: Self-rewriting of the prompt (self-help, SACD loop: detect, analyse, rewrite) debiases better than awareness prompts or few-shot examples; few-shot contrastive debiasing can break instruction following.
agent_test: Add a prompt-rewrite step and measure bias gap and accuracy, not only the gap.
gap_search_note: SACD wins on bias gap (d11) but is not token-matched and measures no accuracy; d08 finds warnings and self-debiasing not significant while an axiom-elicitation step cuts sensitivity 51%; d12 finds generic debiasing backfires on judgment biases (-4.4%).

claim: Reflexion and multi-agent debate amplified bias in SACD tests, and prompt-only defences were weak or backfired on some models in code-review cue attacks.
agent_test: Compare debate vs single-agent rewrite on biased prompts at equal tokens.
gap_search_note: Now three papers: Oh et al. (strategic games, majority amplification), Ma et al. (judge debate, 0.82 to 0.71 consistency), SACD tables. Reflexion-specific evidence still only SACD.

claim: Naming the bias in advance (AwaRe) helped some biases, social-perspective prompting did little and worsened bandwagon; effect depends on the bias.
agent_test: Test generic vs named-bias warnings; log per bias.
gap_search_note: d02: rationality appeals +6.5 to +14.9 points but overattribution worse; d08: bias warning alone 10.3% vs 12.9% control, not significant per bias.

claim: LLM judges show order, bandwagon, salience (length) and self-preference biases (order bias in 11 of 15 models, bandwagon over 70%).
agent_test: Swap candidate order and strip popularity statistics in our judging step; measure flip rate.

claim: Framing, anchoring and halo cues change code-model and code-review behaviour with the code held fixed (Codex copies framing line 62-93%; recall gap framing 33.2%).
agent_test: Test our agent on fixed-code tasks with misleading author or goal text.
gap_search_note: Software-engineering dilemmas (d07, d08) and search agents (d15) show the same cue-driven flips on non-synthetic tasks.

claim: Allowing abstention plus telling the model to inspect for bias traps lifts bias-trap accuracy (GPT-4 33.2 to 79.0 without abstain).
agent_test: Add an abstain option and bias-inspection prompt; check accuracy on valid and total votes.

claim: CRT performance in humans reflects more consistent use of one inference process rather than two qualitatively different systems.
agent_test: Low priority; no direct agent test.

claim: Frontier and reasoning models in 2025-26 still show anchoring, representativeness and plausible-anchor effects on novel or synthetic items, but irrelevant anchors and classic framing are largely resisted; no source tested current top-tier models with contamination control.
schema_part: G (anchor and base-rate checks; source check on numbers read from tools)
agent_test: Run a novel-variant anchor and base-rate probe on our own model at equal tokens.

claim: Prompt-only debiasing is bias-specific: generic warnings, self-check and CoT often do nothing or backfire on judgment biases, while ignore-instructions, evidence-first estimation and axiom elicitation help; no study compared these at equal tokens with accuracy measured.
agent_test: Compare ignore-number, axiom-elicitation and CoT at equal tokens on accuracy plus bias gap.

claim: On agent-like tasks (software engineering decisions, search), bias cues change decisions with the task logic fixed, and the cost rises with number of reasoning steps for confirmation and framing; first evidence order and dead-end history lower the chance of changing course.
schema_part: G and O (forced change-path after failed attempts)
agent_test: Add a dead-end history and a wrong-hint condition to our planning tests.

claim: Stated (verbalised) confidence does not reliably flag a trustworthy first answer: very high mean confidence with weak confidence-correctness correlation (r up to 0.175) in four 2025 models.
schema_part: G (do not gate on stated confidence alone)
agent_test: Compare stated confidence, sample agreement and a regularity check as gates for skipping deliberation.

claim: Natural-frequency formats help Bayesian reasoning in humans but are moderated by format details and design; incentives slightly reduce the conjunction fallacy (d = 0.19). No large preregistered replication of Linda-type rates and no LLM test of natural frequencies were found.
agent_test: Test counts-out-of-1000 restatement of base-rate problems on our agent.

claim: Bias measurements for LLMs are unstable across paraphrase, session and model version, so one-prompt bias scores should not drive design choices.
agent_test: Report bias gaps over at least 3 paraphrases and 5 repeats with the model version pinned.
